books.section: Topic 6.6 The Rise of Industrial Capitalism
America Transformed into the Industrial Giant

options.text: Supporters of Social Darwinism who defended inequality as natural
Union members who wanted higher wages and better conditions

options.misconception: Advocates for lower tariffs would challenge Carnegie.
options.text: Advocates for lower tariffs on imported goods

rationales.A: Industrialists who supported laissez-faire would largely agree with Carnegie's defense of inequality.
rationales.B: Supporters of Social Darwinism defended inequality as natural, close to Carnegie's view.
rationales.C: Union members argued workers deserved fair wages and conditions in the first place, not charity after exploitation. Carnegie's gospel asked the rich to give back; unions asked that workers be paid fairly to begin with.
rationales.D: Tariffs are not the core dispute over wealth and labor.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what Carnegie offers workers. Philanthropy after the fact, not higher wages.
2. Ask who would reject that bargain. Workers who want fair pay and conditions now.
3. Test the others. Laissez-faire industrialists and Social Darwinists largely agree with Carnegie; tariffs miss the point.
4. Match the challenger. The challenge comes from labor, not from Carnegie's allies.
Remember: the sharpest challenge to an idea comes from the people it leaves out.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain excerpt from Carnegie, “The Gospel of Wealth” (1889) with the Keppler 1889 Puck cartoon
stem: Which of the following groups would have been most likely to challenge Carnegie’s perspective?

stimulus.source_note: Andrew Carnegie, “The Gospel of Wealth,” 1889, public domain. Cartoon: Joseph Keppler, “The Bosses of the Senate,” Puck, January 23, 1889, Library of Congress.
stimulus.text: “The problem of our age is the proper administration of wealth, so that the ties of brotherhood may still bind together the rich and poor in harmonious relationship. . . . The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.”
